title: Double Option Nesting (Over-Wrapped Options)
pattern: Nesting an `Option` directly inside another `Option` without separate semantic reasons.
why_bad: Forces downstream code to execute highly complex, nested match blocks (`Some(Some(x))`, `Some(None)`, `None`) with no added safety.
detection: Variables or signatures declared with nested `Option<Option<T>>` types.
counterexample: Representing situations where 'no value provided' (outer None) is distinct from 'explicitly set to empty' (inner None).
fix: Flatten the type to a single `Option<T>` or define a custom enum with clear semantic variant names.
